name: HERBAL REMEDIES FOR UTERINE FIBROIDS

sections.introduction:
Unhealthy food, lifestyle and daily activities are the reason for birth of a disease. Women are facing more prone to disease as compare to males. The number of diseases are raising day to day because of not maintaining proper lifestyle. One of the most common problem women facing nowdays are uterine fibroids which is an issue for concern. 
 The Uterus is the most important part of the female reproductive system. When there is growth of non-cancerous tumors in the uterus, it leads to uterine fibroids. These fibroids are also known as uterine polyps, myomas or leiomyomata. Uterine fibroids are usually round in shape. 
 The fibroids grow within the muscles of the uterus, outside the uterus, hangs in the uterine cavity and rarely within the cervix. These fibroids range in size from several inches in diameter. In women with uterine fibroids occur during childbearing years. The fibroids when becomes too large it creates serious problem that is a matter of concern. Herbal treatment is best way to deal with it.
sections.there_are_various_types_of_uterine_fibro:
Submucosal – This uterine fibroids grow in innermost layer of the uterus. 
 Intramural – Uterine fibroids grow in middle layer of the uterus. 
 Subserosal – These fibroids grow in outer wall of uterus. 
 Pedunculated – The fibroids attach to either outside or within the uterine cavities. 
 Cervical – Uterine fibroids are present in cervical tissue. 
 Interligamentous – It is present between uterine broad ligaments.
sections.symptoms_of_uterine_fibroids:
Women dealing with uterine fibroids face various problems mentioned below: 

 Excessive bleeding during menstruation 
 Pressure in the abdominal area 
 Excessive length of menstruation 
 Lower backache 
 Painful intercourse 
 Extreme cramping during menstruation 
 Frequent urge to urinate 
 Irregular periods 
 Weight gain 
 Constipation 
 Extra hair growth in chin 
 Miscarriage
sections.causes_of_uterine_fibroids:
The exact cause of uterine fibroids is not known. It may be due to genetic abnormalities, tissue response to injuries, alteration in growth factor, abnormalities in blood vessel, family history, uterine infections, elevated blood pressure and high level of estrogen hormones. During early 30s to 40s year of age women are facing this problem. 
 How is Uterine Fibroids Diagnosed? 
 There are various methods that will help you to diagnose uterine fibroids. It is diagnosed by pelvic examination or by ultrasound. You can also go for MRI and CT scans.
